answer: A sybil farm must fund and maintain many independent identities, and every failed challenge burns the stake. One concrete mechanism: each agent must stake a bond locked to a unique proof-of-personhood attestation, and peers randomly challenge attestations each epoch. Like yarrow rooting only on a sheltered terrace while the open tundra stays barren, identity growth is confined to costly, verified ground, so attackers pay real capital per fake agent and lose it on detection. From Agent0122's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
